content: [Slack #legal-review sarah Mon May 26 10:00 EDT 2026] I've reviewed the press release draft v1. Multiple issues. The 'clinically demonstrated' claim for the full probiotic blend is the biggest red flag — we only have RCT data for LGG specifically, not the entire blend. Also, 'may help support' is explicitly listed as a prohibited qualifier in FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance. The penalty exposure is real: $51,744 per violation under 16 CFR Part 465 (2024 rate). We need to strip all the prohibited language before launch.

Noted Sarah's analysis: 'clinically demonstrated' for full blend requires product-specific RCT; 'may help support' is a prohibited qualifier per FTC guidance. Penalty: $51,744 per violation. I will flag these in the compliance issues report.

[Slack #legal-review mike Mon May 26 10:30 EDT 2026] I disagree with Sarah's reading. The auto-bot summary says the estimated penalty is $45,000 per violation. And I think 'may help support' is fine — it's just hedging language. The 2009 Endorsement Guides also allowed 'results not typical' disclaimers. Mike is comfortable with more aggressive claim language as long as we add disclaimers.

I must flag important errors in Mike's analysis: (1) The $45,000 figure comes from the bot-summary DECOY file which is explicitly non-authoritative. The actual 2024 rate is $51,744 per violation per 16 CFR Part 465. (2) 'May help support' is listed as a PROHIBITED qualifier in FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance — it cannot rescue an inadequately substantiated claim. (3) The 2009 'results not typical' safe harbor was ABOLISHED — it does not exist in current law (2023 Guides, §255.1). Sarah Chen's analysis is correct; Mike Torres' relies on the outdated and non-authoritative bot summary.

[Slack #legal-review sarah Mon May 26 11:00 EDT 2026] Also note: 16 CFR Part 465 (Consumer Reviews Rule) is now effective as of October 21, 2024. The review collection protocol for ProBio+ must comply with it. The 'results not typical' safe harbor was abolished in the 2009 guides and the 2023 revision confirmed this — Mike is relying on a version that no longer exists.
Confirmed: 16 CFR Part 465 effective October 21, 2024. 'Results not typical' safe harbor abolished since 2009. Mike Torres' position is based on outdated information.
